verdict.rationale: Jitsu's architecture inherently supports data openness: it's 100% open-source and self-hostable (jitsu-docs-56, jitsu-docs-14), delivers all events directly into your own standard warehouse (Postgres, BigQuery, Snowflake, ClickHouse) as the 'single source of truth' rather than locking data in a proprietary silo (jitsu-docs-21, jitsu-docs-35, jitsu-gh-2), and exposes a full HTTP/OpenAPI management API plus CLI to control and extract configuration (jitsu-docs-61, jitsu-docs-47). This means a user's event data is never trapped — it already lives in open, queryable warehouse formats they own.  Missing for 10: no explicit 'export/backup all data and leave' feature or documentation, no data-portability/migration-out guide, and no independent confirmation of a clean exit process.
